name: @gjsify/spiel-native
description: libspiel, the GNOME Spiel speech-synthesis client library, built as one relocatable shared library plus its typelib so `gi://Spiel` can be imported without a system libspiel — the backend of @gjsify/speech-synthesis. The prebuilt library arrives through per-target optionalDependencies; this package adds only the probe that says where Spiel came from.

osNotes.linux: Builds for linux-x64 and linux-arm64 against the host GLib, GObject, Gio and GStreamer; libspeechprovider is linked statically, so the prebuild is one `.so` with no RUNPATH. `gi://Spiel` loads from the staged directory and `Speaker.new_sync()` reaches the session bus — measured on Fedora 44 / x86_64 with two providers answering. arm64 is built by CI only.
osNotes.darwin: Not built. Spiel is a D-Bus protocol: a client finds providers by their `*.Speech.Provider` well-known names on the session bus and plays their audio through GStreamer. macOS has no session bus and no provider implementation, so a prebuild would load and then find nothing, permanently.
osNotes.win32: Not built, for the same reason as darwin.

scripts.build: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:types
scripts.build:meson: gjsify run init:meson && meson compile -C build
scripts.test: echo 'native only — see test:meson (runs on every prebuild leg)'
